summary: PD-1 reaches further than the triage says: under the default `:strategy auto`, one `not` goal in a clause of the queried relation (at any size), or 256 clauses, sends a query to ATMS, and all three DEFERRED 177 rows then reproduce under a plain `solve` (with 256 clauses, `(big ?name 5)` returns all 256 names where DFS returns one). In-repo programs do not hit it: 12 of 293 auto-routed queries in 17 relational programs take ATMS and all 460 solve lines match DFS; no test pins a wrong answer, and none could catch one. PD-3 holds with an amendment: the race that shows today is on the perf counters (36–180 increments lost per run, `reduce_steps` varying run to run on examples/2026-03-16-track6-acceptance.prologos), while the shared boxes are only read from worker threads (0 `set-box!` in any executor call over 84 programs). PD-2 is not reachable through today's production paths: 0 Tier-1 entries in 76 ATMS query networks built the way production builds them, plus a static bound for the NAF fork. The same detector found a different non-fixpoint: the S1 NAF handler's AND-NOT write to the worldview cache is undone when the projection propagator fires again, and one such re-fire turns light-vehicle's answer into one DFS rejects (new finding W2-4-1). PD-5 is latent: no run in 84 programs or 19 test files goes past 1 outer iteration (the cap raises at the 22nd).

verdicts.question: PD-1 / DEFERRED 177: when does `:strategy auto` pick ATMS (solver.rkt:76-77 and its use); a DFS-against-ATMS answer differential over the relational examples/tests (one .prologos per process, ≤ 20 programs); do existing tests pin a wrong answer?
verdicts.amendment: The reach is wider than 'above the DFS↔ATMS crossover (256)'. `auto` picks ATMS (stratified-eval.rkt:253-293) when four conditions all hold: (1) the queried relation exists; (2) EITHER a clause of one of its own variants carries a `not` or `guard` goal (:265-270), OR its facts + clauses ≥ the threshold 256 (:272-276; solver.rkt:76); (3) no reachable relation has a rule clause with a body-local variable (:292, Rel T1 A.2b scaffolding); (4) no reachable relation has a guard (:293, A.4). Earlier, tier-1-direct-fact-return (:242) answers fact-only queries, and solve-goal-propagator sends 0-arity queries to DFS (relations.rkt:3108-3109). The guard arm of (2) is dead because (4) vetoes it. In practice, therefore, ATMS is chosen by a NAF goal in the queried relation's clauses (at any size) or by ≥ 256 alternatives. One NAF goal is enough to make all three of 177's rows wrong under the default `solve`. In-repo programs do not hit it today. No test pins a wrong answer, and no test has the power to catch one.
verdicts.evidence:
MEASUREMENT (load 3.6–6.9, counts only). Harness w24-run.rkt; STRAT selects current-solver-strategy-override (exported by stratified-eval.rkt; tests use it the same way), ROUTES=1 reads par4-solve-routes. q1-run.sh runs 20 programs × {auto, dfs, atms} with the production executor; compare.py compares answer multisets with gensyms normalised.
(a) Production default. Over 17 relational programs (examples/relational-demo, 2026-04-08-bsp-le-track2, 2026-07-19-rel-t1-acceptance, 2026-03-14-wfle, 2026-03-19-punify, 2026-03-20-punify-p3, 2026-03-18-track7, 2026-03-16-track5/6, 2026-07-31-solve-carrier, 2026-05-08-propagator-demo, dependency-resolver, 2026-07-06-ciu-t6-f1-records, 2026-03-28-sudoku-demo, lib/examples/foray, benchmarks/comparative/atms-adversarial and solve-adversarial), the routes were dfs 195, tier1 86, atms 12 (track7 1, rel-t1 3, atms-adversarial 3, foray 5). Auto against forced DFS: 460 solve lines, 0 answer differences, 6 differing only in order. parity-adversarial aborts in every leg and under tools/scratch-run.sh (DEFERRED 153).
(b) Forced ATMS against DFS on the same 17 programs: 23 lines return an answer DFS rejects, 53 miss answers, 60 hold unresolved or `unknown` values, 10 other (q1-classify.py). Many of the extra answers come from the known A.2b/A.4 scaffolding gaps (guards ignored, body-local variables). One clean in-repo PD-1 case has neither: atms-adversarial.prologos:115 `solve (color-code ?name 5)` gives 10 names under ATMS and `cyan` under DFS. That is the caller's binding being invisible inside the branches (177 mechanisms 1 and 3). Under auto it routes to DFS (10 clauses, no NAF).
(c) Constructed reach, default `solve` with no solver declaration (reach/reach-naf.prologos, .out). `defr tagged [?x ?c] &> (= x 1) (= c 1) (not (blocked x)) &> (= x 2) (= c 2) (not (blocked x))`: `(tagged ?x 1)` gives `@[{:x 2} {:x 1}]`, DFS `@[{:x 1}]`. `two-naf` (`(= x 1) (= x 2) (not ...)`) gives `@[{:x 1}]`, DFS `@[]`. `clash-naf` gives `@[{:x 1, :y 2}]`, DFS `@[]`. The controls agree (unbound `tagged`: order only; `agree-naf`: equal). routes {atms 5, dfs 5}. reach-bigc256.prologos (256 clauses `&> (= name "nK") (= code K)`): `solve (big ?name 5)` returns all 256 names, DFS `{:name "n5"}`; the route is atms. reach-bigc255: DFS route, correct. reach-bigf255/256 (facts only): tier1 route, correct.
(d) Tests. w24-test.rkt dynamic-requires one test module under a global override. Forced DFS gives 0 failures in test-rel-t1-naf (12), test-rel-t1-pol (148), test-relational-e2e (15), test-solve-carrier (50), test-solver-parity (15), test-stratified-eval (18) and test-propagator-solver (13 checks). So no test depends on an answer that only the ATMS route gives. Read by hand: test-solver-parity.rkt's 15 cases contain none of the three 177 shapes (caller binding against a branch write, conflicting unify in one clause, var-var clash). test-propagator-solver.rkt:81-99 calls solve-goal-propagator directly, pins only `length = 1` and membership in a 3-value set, and its titles still say 'last-write-wins without PU'. Those are weak pins, not wrong pins.
verdicts.power_check: C9's c1-overwrite and c4-varvar, run in the same harness and legs, show 2 and 1 auto-vs-DFS differences; the comparator finds the known wrong answers. The forced-ATMS override fails 3/12 (test-rel-t1-naf), 17/148 (test-rel-t1-pol) and 2/15 (test-relational-e2e) tests, so the override reaches those tests and a forced-DFS 0 could have been nonzero. Limits: test-stratified-eval sets the override itself (:53), test-propagator-solver bypasses the dispatcher, and test-solver-parity overrides internally, so for those three the forced-DFS 0 says nothing. The threshold boundary flips between 255 and 256 clauses in the same file shape.

### 177 addendum — REACH MEASURED: `:strategy auto` (the default) sends a query to ATMS whenever the queried relation has a `not` goal in a clause, at any size, or ≥ 256 facts + clauses; all three rows then reproduce under a plain `solve`. No in-repo program hits it today, and no test would catch it.
**Found by** PAR 4 D.3 wave 2, W2-4, at main `c1f389ab` (worktree `par4-arena-executors` @ `07fe9a12`).
**Reproduction** (one file per process): `tools/scratch-run.sh -t 120 reach-naf.prologos`. The file (kept by W2-4) holds `defr blocked [?x] || 99`, `defr tagged [?x ?c] &> (= x 1) (= c 1) (not (blocked x)) &> (= x 2) (= c 2) (not (blocked x))`, `two-naf` = `&> (= x 1) (= x 2) (not (blocked x))` and `clash-naf` = `&> (= x 1) (= y 2) (= x y) (not (blocked x))`. Results: `solve (tagged ?x 1)` → `@[{:x 2} {:x 1}]` (DFS `@[{:x 1}]`); `solve (two-naf ?x)` → `@[{:x 1}]` (DFS `@[]`); `solve (clash-naf ?x ?y)` → `@[{:x 1, :y 2}]` (DFS `@[]`). A relation with 256 clauses `&> (= name "nK") (= code K)` gives `solve (big ?name 5)` → 256 answers (DFS 1); with 255 clauses the answer is correct.
**Reach**: in the dispatcher (stratified-eval.rkt:253-293), ATMS is chosen by a NAF goal in the queried relation's own clauses (:265-270), or by facts + clauses ≥ 256 (:272-276), and in both cases only when no reachable rule clause has a body-local variable (:292) and no reachable relation has a guard (:293). In 17 in-repo relational programs, 12 of 293 routed queries take ATMS and all agree with DFS (460 solve lines, 0 differences). Forced `:strategy atms` over the same programs returns answers DFS rejects on 23 lines, e.g. `benchmarks/comparative/atms-adversarial.prologos:115` `(color-code ?name 5)` gives 10 names instead of 1.
**Tests**: none pins a wrong answer (forced DFS: 0 failures over 7 relational test files; forced ATMS: 22 failures, which is the power). None would catch the three rows: test-solver-parity.rkt has none of the shapes, and test-propagator-solver.rkt:81-99 pins only `length = 1`.
**Fix shape**: unchanged (a, b and c above). **Test layer, now concrete**: add reach-naf's five queries and the 256-clause query to test-solver-parity.rkt as WS-level parity rows (both strategies); tighten test-propagator-solver.rkt:81-99 to the exact answer.
**When**: the default strategy reaches this with one `not` goal, so the 'sooner' option in **When** now applies to `:strategy auto` users, not only to explicit `:strategy atms` users. The owner may want a stopgap: route any NAF query whose relation graph contains a unify of a caller-bound parameter to DFS, until P1a lands.

verdicts.question: PD-3: do fires on today's thread-per-round executor (driver.rkt:567) touch shared mutable state? Reproduce a race or bound it (current-prop-net-box set-box! at resolution.rkt:373/386 via metavar-store.rkt:1063; current-persistent-registry-net-box; meta-store hashes; perf counters; the observer).
verdicts.amendment: C6-1 holds: fires do touch shared mutable state from parallel OS threads today. The race that manifests is on the perf counters (performance-counters.rkt:181-195, `(set-perf-counters-X! pc (add1 (perf-counters-X pc)))`, documented at :3 as 'Deterministic heartbeat counters'). It does not manifest on the shared boxes. Fires lose increments: `PERF-COUNTERS` reduce_steps varies run to run under the default executor, and fires also do extra reduction work. The extra work is CONJECTURE: the cause is probably misses on the shared per-command whnf/nf memo hasheqs (driver.rkt:729-732) when two threads reduce the same term. Workers only READ current-prop-net-box and the registry box. The retry bridge's `set-box!` (resolution.rkt:371-387; installed at driver.rkt:3945; its propagator is at metavar-store.rkt:1063-1065) is live in production code but was seen only on the main thread, in rounds narrower than 8. It would race only if two such fires landed in one wide round; none did in 84 programs and 5 constraint tests. No answer differed in any compared run. The observer and the executor were never called off the main thread: no nested BSP run happened inside a worker-thread fire.
verdicts.evidence:
MEASUREMENT (no rebuild). w24-run.rkt wraps the exported `current-parallel-executor`. RACE=1 parameterizes chaperoned copies of current-prop-net-box and current-persistent-registry-net-box over each executor call; the threads that `make-parallel-thread-fire-all` creates (propagator.rkt:3691-3730, `thread #:pool 'own` at :3715) inherit them. Every unbox and set-box! is logged by thread class, and a set-box! counts as a lost update if its thread did not read the value it overwrites. PERFCHAP=1 chaperones the perf-counter struct's 19 mutators the same way, and per call compares the CAS-counted attempts with the field deltas actually stored, which is an exact count of lost increments.
- Medium tier plus all examples (q2-all.sh, 84 programs, parity-adversarial aborts on DEFERRED 153): 5 192 executor rounds, 805 of them ≥ 8 wide. Worker-thread unbox of prop-net-box 6 435 and of registry-net-box 452. set-box! inside executor calls: 0 on worker threads, 0 on main. Perf increments in executor calls: 3 874 on main, 3 980 on workers (all `reduce-steps`); the largest are 2026-03-16-track6-acceptance at 2 583, track5 at 668, homoiconicity at 238 and track4 at 209.
- examples/2026-03-16-track6-acceptance.prologos, results only: EXEC=seq gave reduce_steps 17 579 in 6 of 6 runs. EXEC=prod gave 17 591, 17 592, 17 592, 17 602, 17 615 and 17 618 (q2/nondet/track6.*.out), and 17 608–17 629 in 10 earlier runs. The normalised result lines have the same md5 in all 12 runs, and every other counter is equal.
- Instrumented (PERFCHAP): seq made 3 313 attempts in executor calls and lost 0. Prod lost 53, 59, 36, 89, 52 and 180 increments in six runs (q2/nondet/track6-perfchap-lost.out). track5 gives 9 874–9 887 under prod against 9 873 under seq.
- Constraint tests through w24-test-race.rkt: test-constraint-postponement makes 2 set-box! on prop-net-box and test-constraint-readiness makes 6, all on the main thread, and neither has a round with a worker-thread set. The other three (test-constraint-inference, test-constraint-chain-01, test-perf-counters) make no set-box! at all.
- Heavy files: results and PERF-COUNTERS are identical in 10 prod and 2 seq runs of constraints-adversarial, nat-arithmetic and type-adversarial (13, 5 and 7 worker increments). Low contention, so no loss was observed there.
verdicts.power_check: q2/q2-power.rkt runs 16 propagators in one round on the production executor `(make-parallel-thread-fire-all)`. Each fire does 20 000 unbox/set-box! read-modify-writes on `(current-prop-net-box)` (the retry bridge's shape) and 20 000 `perf-inc-reduce!`. Out of 320 000 expected, the three runs lose 275 097, 277 194 and 284 634 box updates and 287 454, 289 445 and 281 331 counter increments. Under sequential-fire-all both totals are exactly 320 000. At ITER = 1, nothing is lost in any run (q2-power-iter1.out), so loss needs contention, which explains why the heavy files show none. The lost-increment instrument reads 0 for every seq run and 36–180 for prod, so it can tell the executors apart.
verdicts.deferred_text:
### NNN. ⬜ THE PRODUCTION THREAD EXECUTOR RACES ON THE PERF COUNTERS TODAY — `PERF-COUNTERS` (documented as 'deterministic heartbeat counters') varies run to run under the default executor: `examples/2026-03-16-track6-acceptance.prologos` gives reduce_steps 17 591–17 629 against 17 579 sequential, with 36–180 increments lost per run
**Found by** PAR 4 D.3: C6-1 claimed that fires race on shared state; wave 2's W2-4 measured it at main `c1f389ab`.
**Mechanism** (read in code): driver.rkt:567 installs `make-parallel-thread-fire-all`, which fires every round of ≥ 8 propagators on fresh `thread #:pool 'own` OS threads (propagator.rkt:3691-3730). The fires inherit the command's parameterization, so they share the per-command perf-counter struct and the whnf/nf/nat-value memo hasheqs (driver.rkt:729-732). `perf-inc-*` is a non-atomic field read-modify-write (performance-counters.rkt:181-195).
**Reproduction**: run the file with the default executor and with `(current-parallel-executor sequential-fire-all)` injected (W2-4's `w24-run.rkt`, EXEC=prod|seq); sequential gives the same count every run. Power fixture: 16 parallel fires doing 20 000 increments each lose about 88 % (sequential 0).
**Reach**: in 84 programs (examples/, lib/examples/, benchmarks/comparative), fires made 3 980 counter increments off the main thread, in 24 files. No answer differed in any compared run. The shared boxes are only read from workers: 6 887 unboxes and 0 `set-box!` over 805 wide rounds. The constraint-retry bridge's `set-box!` (resolution.rkt:386, installed at driver.rkt:3945) is live: test-constraint-postponement makes 2 and test-constraint-readiness 6, but only in narrow rounds on the main thread. If two such fires land in one wide round, the last writer would overwrite the elab-network's cell-info / next-meta-id / id-map / meta-info.
**Consequences**: bench tooling that treats PERF-COUNTERS as deterministic (counter A/Bs, corpus-compare) sees noise on any file with wide rounds, and the duplicated memo work is real CPU.
**Fix shape**: delete the thread executor (PAR 4 O-14 / P0.5; it is also 1.4–1.6× slower, CL-2). If any parallel executor survives, counters become per-executor and are summed at the barrier (CL-9's per-executor fuel shape), and the retry bridge stops writing `current-prop-net-box` from a fire: its effect goes through cells (CL-13; the D.3 W2-5 census).
**When**: P0.5.

verdicts.question: PD-2 / DEFERRED 178: how far does production reach the Tier-1 non-fixpoint? Bound it statically (the five relations.rkt sites) and dynamically with a generic non-fixpoint detector (after run-to-quiescence returns, re-fire every propagator once; report changed cells) applied to the relational examples; power row: C2's Tier-1 probe must be flagged.
verdicts.amendment: The defect is real (C2's network: B = 0, flagged), but today's production paths cannot reach the shape that drops a dependent. (1) Every top-level query network carries the worldview projection propagator on its worklist. make-solver-context installs it per query (atms.rkt:237, then install-worldview-projection, propagator.rkt:978-987, a plain net-add-propagator), so Tier 1's all-fire-once predicate is false. (2) The NAF S1 fork (relations.rkt:271-283) installs the inner goal over FRESH inner-scope cells (build-var-env at :278); ground and resolved arguments become values. A Tier-1 flush there writes only cells with no dependents. (3) Four of the five sites (relations.rkt:2148, 2161, 2183, 2699) take the fire-once path only when current-worldview-bitmask ≠ 0 (:2141, :2154, :2176), that is, inside an assumption branch. solver-assume writes cell 1 eagerly (atms.rkt:276-282), which excludes Tier 1. The fifth (:2636, single viable fact) is unconditional, but falls under (1) and (2). Fix 178 before P2 anyway: D.2 relies on run results being fixpoints. Method limit: no exported hook sees a Tier-1 flush at run time. It emits no observer record (178 / DEFERRED 176 item 4), and an instrumented copy of propagator.rkt cannot link without a rebuild. The NAF-fork case therefore rests on the static bound, which is CONJECTURE-grade for that one path.
verdicts.evidence:
Static census (code reading) plus MEASUREMENT.
Static: census-fireonce.sh, on production files only (tests, benchmarks, tools, compiled and examples excluded). There are 30 net-add-fire-once-propagator call sites. The only ones that pass literal empty inputs are relations.rkt:2148, 2161, 2183, 2636 and 2699. :2353 passes `input-cids` with outputs '(), so it has nothing to drop. No other production `#:flags` callers exist, and the elab/metavar/driver wrappers (metavar-store.rkt:542, 562; driver.rkt:1720; typing-propagators.rkt) all pass non-empty inputs. Tier 1 is decided only at the entry of run-to-quiescence-bsp (propagator.rkt:3410-3445). Installs inside a fire or a handler run inside the Tier-2 loop, which never re-checks Tier 1.
Dynamic, on the production construction path (q3-tier1-sweep.rkt). For one file per process, the sweep processes it, then builds a solver network for every relation in the resulting store exactly as solve-goal-propagator does (relations.rkt:3077-3158, through module->namespace on the same module instances). It builds two queries per relation: all variables free, and argument 1 bound to the first fact's value. On each net3 it evaluates the Tier-1 predicate, runs `run-to-quiescence`, and re-fires every propagator on the result with fire-and-collect-writes (sandboxed boxes, counters off). Across 16 files (15 relational programs plus reach-naf) that is 184 queries: 86 answered by tier-1-direct-fact-return, 22 sent to DFS as 0-arity, and 76 network runs. Of those 76, 0 entered Tier 1 and 76 went through Tier 2. The post-run detector flagged 13 Tier-2 results; all are W2-4-1 (12 on cell 1) or W2-4-2 (foray `truths`). wfle-acceptance and punify-acceptance timed out at 120 s and were not swept.
In-run detector (w24-run.rkt NONFIX=1, solver networks). It runs at every observed S0 quiescence and at every round entry, re-firing the propagators that are not on the worklist. Under auto, 10 files give 28 entry points and 14 quiescence points with 0 flagged. Under forced ATMS: 243 entry and 141 quiescence points; the flags are the cell-1 states (rel-t1, foray) and foray `truths`.
verdicts.power_check: In the same detector code (q3-tier1-sweep.rkt prints it first), C2's network (d3-wave1/C2/probe-tier1.rkt construction) reads 'tier1-eligible #t, B = 0, non-fixpoint propagators ((0 (21)))': propagator 0 would change cell 21 = B. The Tier-2 control reads 'tier1-eligible #f, B = 7, ()'. The detector also fires on production solver networks (the W2-4-1 and W2-4-2 flags), so it can see non-fixpoints there. A Tier-1 0 is therefore a measured 0 on 76 production query networks. The NAF-fork path stays unmeasured (method limit above).

### 178 addendum — REACH: none through today's flows (bounded; latent); still fix in P0.5
**Found by** PAR 4 D.3 wave 2 (W2-4), main `c1f389ab`.
**Static bound**: Tier 1 is decided only at entry to `run-to-quiescence-bsp` (propagator.rkt:3410-3445). verdicts.question: PD-5: does any example or test drive the strata outer loop (propagator.rkt:3619-3634) past 10 iterations?
verdicts.amendment: Answer: no. The cap is latent today: the maximum is 1 outer iteration. The cap raises a plain `error` once a stratum handler produces S0 work at outer-round > 20 (propagator.rkt:3619 for the value tier inside process-tier, :3631 for the topology tier). A run can therefore complete 21 outer iterations after the first, and the 22nd raises. That is C8's 'depth 23 raises'. Whether the exception escapes process-file the way DEFERRED 153's DFS depth error does is not measured.
verdicts.evidence:
MEASUREMENT. The instrument (w24-run.rkt OUTER=1, w24-test-outer.rkt) needs no rebuild. It sets current-bsp-observer, and replaces each entry of propagator.rkt's `stratum-handlers` box (reached through module->namespace; the handlers themselves are unchanged) with a wrapper that records, on entry, the run that owns the network. Runs are chained by the fuel cell: a round's input fuel is its output fuel plus the number of pids, and the merge does not write fuel. A round-0 record continues a run only when a wrapped handler has just produced S0 work on a network with that fuel. Capturing the run at handler entry keeps nested runs on forks that share the fuel value from breaking the chain. A first version without that capture linked 15 of 26 continuations; it was corrected and re-run.
Results: q4-run.sh over all 85 .prologos files under examples/, lib/examples/ and benchmarks/comparative/ (84 ran; parity-adversarial aborts on DEFERRED 153). 2 511 BSP runs; outer-round histogram {0: 2 485, 1: 26}. Handlers were called 219 times and produced S0 work 26 times; all 26 continuations were linked, with 0 unlinked rounds. Files reaching 1: 2026-03-16-track4/5/6-acceptance, 2026-03-18-track7, 2026-03-25-track10b and 2026-03-26-ppn-track0. Tests (q4-tests.sh, 19 files chosen to stress the strata: tabling ×3, narrowing ×3, trait/method resolution ×4, retraction, structural decomposition, union-types-atms, classify-inhabit, readiness, rel-t1-naf, rel-t1-pol, constraint-postponement, relational-e2e): maximum 1, reached by test-narrowing-01 (8 runs) and test-union-types-atms (10 runs). The instrument therefore reports > 10 when a run reaches it, and the corpus maximum of 1 is a measured value. All 26 handler-produced continuations in the corpus were linked.

### NNN. ⬜ THE STRATA OUTER LOOP RAISES A PLAIN `error` AT A FIXED CAP OF 20 OUTER ITERATIONS (propagator.rkt:3619, :3631) — latent today (maximum 1 iteration in 2 511 runs); reachable once SLG table discovery goes through topology requests (BC-3)
**Found by** PAR 4 D.3: C8 (C8-4) found it; W2-4 measured the reach, at main `c1f389ab`.
**Reproduction**: C8's `benchmarks/par4/d3-wave1/C8/probe-outer-cap.rkt`. It builds a chain of N propagators, each of which requests the next through `callback-topology-request` (cell 6). N ≤ 22 completes; N = 23 raises `run-to-quiescence-bsp: stratum handlers: >20 outer iterations — possible infinite loop`.
**Reach today**: none. Maximum outer-round 1 over 2 511 BSP runs in the 84 programs under examples/, lib/examples/ and benchmarks/comparative/ (26 runs reach 1), and 1 over 19 strata-heavy test files.
**Why it matters**: BC-3 (PAR 4 D.2 §11) and BSP-LE Track 3 send every new call variant's table/producer through the topology tier, so the discovery depth becomes the number of outer iterations. A recursion 22 variants deep would raise, and a counter of handler activations is not a termination argument (CL-9).
**Fix shape**: replace the counter with a per-run budget held on the network (CL-9's fuel per epoch, summed at the boundary). Exhausting it writes a contradiction or 'fuel-exhausted' fact, not an exception, and the bound is a declared measure (topology growth is monotone in cell and propagator ids, so it is finite for a finite program). findings.claim_attacked: That a production run-to-quiescence result is a fixpoint of its own S0 propagators, so that a non-fixpoint or replay monitor reads 0 on correct runs and a re-run of S0 cannot change an answer. The NAF handler's comment says 'If provable → nogood for h_naf … tagged writes under h_naf become invisible' (relations.rkt:346-353).
findings.evidence:
MEASUREMENT. The S1 NAF handler process-naf-request (relations.rkt:206-354) records a NAF failure as an AND-NOT read-modify-write directly on the worldview cache, cell 1 (:240 per-binding path; :350-353 shared-bit path; the S0 guard does the same at :2346-2349, which is DEFERRED 157(b)). It does not write the decisions cell that cell 1 is projected from. Cell 1 has a second writer: the worldview projection propagator that make-solver-context installs on every query network (atms.rkt:237; propagator.rkt:978-987, which reads decisions cell 20 and writes cell 1 with a replacement merge). After the run, the projection's output disagrees with cell 1.
q3-tier1-sweep.rkt, over 76 ATMS query networks built on the production path, flags 12 results, all from relations with `not` goals: safe-twohop, safe-reach, fruit-not-of-color(2), light-vehicle, unreachable-from-a, reachable, ancestor-e. In each, propagator 0 would change cell 1.
q3-cell1.rkt on examples/2026-07-19-rel-t1-acceptance.prologos `light-vehicle` (`&> (vehicle v) (not (license v))`): cell 1 is 0b11 after the run and 0b111 after one re-fire of propagator 0. Answers from the result: `{v0: "bicycle"}`, which equals DFS and production. Answers after S0 re-fires propagator 0: `{"automobile"} {"bicycle"}`, an answer DFS rejects.
The in-run detector also flags such states at round entry (forced ATMS: 2 in rel-t1, 2 in foray), i.e. while S0 continues after the S1 handler. Today's answers are right only because nothing re-fires the projection once the handler has run. None of the 12 queries that auto routes to ATMS in the repo hit it (0 flags under auto).
findings.direction: Write invalidation as growth, the way DEFERRED 157's measured fix shape does, extended to the S1 handler. NAF and guard verdicts go into an `ior` invalidated-bits cell, or are written as nogoods into the decisions cell that the projection reads. The projection propagator then derives worldview = committed ∧ ¬invalidated, so cell 1 has one writer and the S1 result is a fixpoint. This is the same split as CL-6's 'cell 1 becomes a derived projection α(decisions, nogoods)'. After the change, the generic detector must read 0 on the 12 flagged queries and light-vehicle must stay `{bicycle}` after a forced re-fire. PAR 4's replay/non-fixpoint monitor needs this before it can have a zero baseline on solver networks, and at K > 1 or under DIRECT an interleaving that re-fires the projection after the handler would produce the wrong answer.
findings.falsifier: A run in which re-firing propagator 0 after the S1 handler leaves cell 1 unchanged for a provable NAF goal. Or a proof that no scheduler PAR 4 plans (DIRECT, K > 1, the replay) ever fires the projection again after the S1 handler within one query.
findings.confidence: high (mechanism and the light-vehicle flip); medium (production reach: latent today)

findings.claim_attacked: That BSP's handling of undeclared writes (direct set in bulk-merge-writes) loses nothing on production solver networks
findings.evidence: MEASUREMENT. lib/examples/foray.prologos `defr truths [?b1 ?b2 ?b3 ?b4] &> (bool b1) (bool b2) (bool b3) (bool b4)`, forced through the ATMS construction path (q3-cell1.rkt PID=6, q3/cell26-truths.out). Propagators 6 and 7 (flags 0, input cell 31, NO declared outputs) write the query scope cell 26 as an undeclared write when re-fired, adding an entry `(3 . {v2 1})` that the run's result lacks. The production ATMS answer is 1 binding map with v2 and v3 unresolved; DFS gives 16. This is DEFERRED 157(a)'s class (undeclared writes applied by direct set) with a measured answer consequence. Not reachable under auto today: the clause has no NAF, so `truths` routes to DFS. Which install site creates propagators 6 and 7 is not pinned. CONJECTURE: the tabling consumer, since rules table by default; 157 lists relations.rkt:2824.
findings.direction: 157(a)'s fix: declare the scope cells as outputs, so the write goes through the merge. Add `truths` (both strategies) to the parity rows.
findings.falsifier: Re-firing propagators 6 and 7 on the result changes nothing once their outputs are declared, and the answer set equals DFS's 16 — or shows that the remaining gap is A.2b's tabling seam rather than the lost write.

findings.claim_attacked: That a run-boundary or Tier-1 trap can be added without a rebuild
findings.evidence: MEASUREMENT. No exported parameter runs at the entry or exit of run-to-quiescence-bsp. The executor and observer are read there but called only per round, and Tier 1 calls neither. Loading an instrumented copy of propagator.rkt under its own module name (mk-inst.py, inst-loader.rkt, t1-inst.rkt; nothing written to disk) fails with `instantiate-linklet: mismatch; reference to a variable that is not exported name: net-new-cell-widen158.1 … importing instance: reduction.rkt`. Keyword procedures export gensym'd core names that change with every compilation, so this route always needs a rebuild of the dependents.
findings.direction: Have Tier 1 emit an observer record (DEFERRED 176 item 4) and export a run-boundary hook, (enter net tier) and (exit net result), that defaults to off. Both cost a branch on a box. Without them, every PAR 4 'is path X reached?' question about run boundaries needs an env-gated build (W2-2's mechanism).
findings.falsifier: An exported hook that observes Tier-1 flushes at run time in an unmodified build.
